answer: node2vec exploits graph structure by generating biased random walks that mix breadth-first and depth-first exploration, so it learns embeddings from node co-occurrence patterns in sampled neighborhoods and can capture both local and more global structural roles. LINE(2nd), by contrast, does not use random walks; it directly preserves second-order proximity by making nodes with similar neighborhood distributions have similar embeddings, typically through an objective based on observed edge co-occurrence/conditional neighborhood similarity. In short, node2vec uses walk-based context sampling to encode structure, while LINE(2nd) uses a direct second-order neighborhood-preservation objective.
